citations.claim: pre-impact speed just before floor contact
post-impact speed exceeds 0.9*incident speed, showing super-elastic impulse
first violating step energy exceeds allowed 68.55 (E0 57.77)

counterfactual.change: changed bodies[0].e from 0.9 to 0 (single field). Inelastic bounce removes energy gain; same dt/steps/gravity passes energy_bound, confirming restitution-dependent energy injection is causal.

explanation: Shrunk to single bouncing ball (r=0.5,m=1,e=0.9) falling under gravity onto arena floor (implicit boundary). Energy is conserved ~57.76 J until impact. Between step 62 (y=0.508, vy=-10.27) and step 63 (y=0.5, vy=+12.34) collision response injects energy: rebound speed / incident speed = 12.34/10.27 ≈1.20 exceeds declared restitution 0.9, so kinetic energy jumps from ~57.76 to 81.03 J (+40%), exceeding 10%+5J tolerance (limit 68.55). Likely collision impulse and/or positional correction adds velocity instead of scaling by e, or gravity impulse is double-counted in substep, causing super-elastic bounce.
vision_note: Across tiles 60-62 the single blue circle falls straight down toward the black floor line, closing the small gap each step. At tile 63 it is in contact with the floor at the reported violation instant, with no other bodies, walls or waypoints visible and no obvious tunneling or wall penetration.
